gerthardus-lodewikus-booysen.r: THE ONE DOCUMENT THAT NAMES HIM HAS BEEN WEAKENED, AND BY SOMEBODY WHO HAD NOT SEEN IT. On 14 September 2026 PIETER VAN ZYL, answering this archive’s G2G question, guessed that the 1876 informant had reached for a name already in the household — and added, from memory, that he thought a CHILD of Petrus Jacobus was called Gerhardus Lodewicus. HE IS RIGHT, AND THE CHILD IS ON THE SAME SHEET: line 12 of that very notice names JAN GERTHARDUS LODEWIKUS BOOIJSEN among the eight children. So the name this archive takes from LINE 3, for the dead man’s FATHER, is the back half of his SON’S name, eight lines below, in one clerk’s hand — and the half that is dropped, JAN, is the name de Villiers gives as the real father. THIS DOES NOT PROVE THE FATHER WAS JAN and this archive is not swapping one unproved father for another. It removes the only document that has ever carried this name from the evidence for him. The top of the male line is now held up by less than it was this morning. He still has no birth date, no death date, and no parents: the oldest open question on this site is about him. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND THE LAST ESCAPE ROUTE IS CLOSED. This archive's standing objection was that de Villiers's 1893 original was revised by Pama in 1981, and a revision can move a man; if the 1981 edition had relocated Petrus Jacobus, the death notice would stand. RIËL SMIT, WHO HAS THE 1981 EDITION: “Yes, DE VILLIERS & PAMA (1981) STILL PLACE PETRUS JACOBUS (b3c4d7) b. 21 SEPT 1788 UNDER JAN b3c4.” Pieter van Zyl adds that he SEARCHED FOR A MARRIAGE BETWEEN A GERHARDUS LODEWICUS AND A MAGDALENA DE BEER AND COULD NOT FIND ONE. FOUR THINGS NOW POINT ONE WAY and the only thing pointing the other is line 3 of Notice 678. THE SPINE IS STILL NOT BEING MOVED ON THIS: everything against him is a printed genealogy agreeing with its own earlier edition, and what he has is a primary document signed by a son. WHAT ENDS IT IS THE BAPTISM ENTRY OF 21 SEPTEMBER 1788 — the register de Villiers compiled his entry from, naming the father in a contemporary hand. It is now the first item on the errands page.

jan-booijsen.r: THE MAN THE BOOK PUTS WHERE THE DOCUMENT PUTS SOMEBODY ELSE. b3c4 — son of Gerrit Booijsen and Johanna du Rand; burgher at Drakenstein; MARRIED MAGDALENA DE BEER 21 JANUARY 1770 and remarried MARGARETHA PRETORIUS 15 DECEMBER 1793, which is how this archive knows the de Beer wife was dead by then. De Villiers (1893) gives him twelve children, of whom d5 is JAN JONATHAN, d6 MAGDALENA and d7 PETRUS JACOBUS, BAPTISED 21 SEPTEMBER 1788 — this archive's own ancestor. RIËL SMIT CONFIRMS THAT DE VILLIERS & PAMA (1981) STILL PLACES HIM THERE. Pieter van Zyl notes he was dead more than forty years before Petrus Jacobus died in 1876, which is why the grandson who signed the death notice could write somebody else's name in the parents' box. HE IS ENTERED AS INFERRED AND NOT AS DOCUMENTED, because two editions of one printed genealogy are one source agreeing with itself, and the primary document on this site says Gerthardus Lodewikus. The baptism register of 21 September 1788 decides between them.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The decisive one failed in an informative way: the 1788 baptism that names Petrus Jacobus's father does not surface, because the date filters are ignored and the 18th-century Cape registers are not name-indexed — a negative about the index, not the register. Two other entries independently confirmed de Villiers on two of Jan Booijsen's sons, which strengthens the book against the death notice. And the relationship search on the father, queued as Question 13, returned a household: John Augustus Barry II had a wife and nine children this archive had never seen, including the Kolbe name carried into a fourth generation.

jan-jonathan-booijsen.r: b3c4d5 — the eldest of the three siblings whose marriages braid this family into the Viljoens. Burgher at Graaff-Reinet; MARRIED 28 MAY 1797 to JUDITH CORNELIA THERESIA VILJOEN, three months after his sister Magdalena married that woman's brother Hercules Albertus. A BROTHER AND A SISTER MARRIED A SISTER AND A BROTHER IN ONE YEAR. Seven children, and the sixth is JUDITH CORNELIA THERESIA, BAPTISED 16 AUGUST 1807 — b3c4d5e6, the code this archive resolved last week to settle a Johannesburg gravestone. She carries her mother's three names entire, and her mother was a Viljoen.

adriana-christina-viljoen.r: His wife, married at CRADOCK on 3 November 1828—FROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ—and named with him on their daughter Anna Maria's baptism of 13 September 1835 — a daughter called after his mother, which is how this archive knows the naming ran that way in this generation too. AND SHE WAS PROBABLY HIS FIRST COUSIN. De Villiers, volume 3, under VILLION, thans VILJOEN: “(e) 12 HERCULES ALBERTUS, gedoopt 30 Maart 1777, burger te Graaff-Reinet, GEHUWD 26 FEBRUARI 1797 MET MAGDALENA BOOIJSEN”, and their seventh child is “ADRIANA CHRISTINA, GEDOOPT 19 AUGUSTUS 1810”. Magdalena Booijsen is b3c4d6, the SISTER of Petrus Jacobus — David Schalk's own father. That makes Adriana Christina eighteen in 1828 and makes him her first cousin. NOT PROVED: de Villiers records her baptism and GIVES HER NO HUSBAND, and the 1828 Cradock date is itself only on WikiTree. Right name, right age, right district, and a family already tied twice — but the weak join is the marriage record this archive has never seen.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Magdalena Booijsen married Hercules Albertus Viljoen in February; her brother Jan Jonathan married Hercules Albertus’s sister Judith Cornelia Theresia in May. Two households became one twice over in a single year. Thirty-one years later, David Schalk Booijzen — son of the third of those children — married Adriana Christina Viljoen at Cradock on 3 November 1828. Magdalena Booijsen’s seventh child is Adriana Christina, baptised 19 August 1810 , which makes her eighteen in 1828 and makes him her first cousin : his father and her mother were brother and sister. What is proved and what is not. De Villiers records Adriana Christina Viljoen’s baptism and gives her no husband .

jan-gerthardus-lodewikus-booijsen.r: Fifth on his father’s 1876 notice, and named for the man at the top of the line. HIS is the estate TAB MHG O/2899, which this archive had spent months attributing to his nephew of the same name born in 1855 — the Transvaal probate index gives him as the deceased, aged 67, born district Graaff-Reinet, died 25 May 1885 at Vaalbank in the district of Lichtenburg. His daughter Magdalena Susanna Maria died on the same farm in 1920, and her death notice names him. He is how this family reaches the western Transvaal.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: Pieter van Zyl had already searched for a marriage between a Gerhardus Lodewicus and a Magdalena de Beer and found none, and remembered — correctly — that a CHILD of Petrus Jacobus carried the name. He is on line 12 of the same sheet: Jan Gerthardus Lodewikus Booijsen. The name in the parents' box is the back half of a son's name, and the half that was dropped is the father's. BOTH LETTERS WENT OUT THE SAME MORNING: a short thanks to Ms Xaba asking only whether MHG 52653 is a valid reference, and a first approach to the private researcher — what she charges and how, her view on whether the work is worth doing at all, and an offer to start with one file.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The date had no source except the file number. The Transvaal probate index names the estate's deceased in full: Jan Gerardus Lodewicus Booijzen, aged 67, born district Graaff-Reinet, died 25 May 1885 at Vaalbank, district Lichtenburg — born about 1818, which is his UNCLE, fifth on the 1876 Sterfkennis. The nephew's death date is withdrawn and nothing is known about what became of him. The particular error is worth naming: the archive read a year off a reference number, wrote it in as a fact, and then cited the fact back.

magdalena-susanna-maria-van-den-berg.n: Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg
magdalena-susanna-maria-van-den-berg.r: His daughter, and the first person in the western Transvaal this archive can attach to the line rather than merely set beside it. Her 1920 Sterfkennis — estate 44420, stamped Pretoria 16 August 1920 — names her parents as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen and Magdalena Susanna Maria, gives her age as 59 years 9 months, and lists seven children. Her son-in-law B. J. van den Berg signed it.

pages.t: Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: Lichtenburg joins the line Found found The same correction does the opposite favour. Vaalbank, in the district of Lichtenburg, is where the 1876 man's son died in 1885 — and this archive had already read a 1920 Sterfkennis from that farm for Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg, born Booyzen about 1860, father entered as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen, filed under “NOT PROVED”. She is his daughter. Two deaths on one farm thirty-five years apart, which is settlement rather than passage. Read west along the atlas: Rustenburg 1876, Lichtenburg 1885 and 1920, Marico 1903.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The direct ancestor died in district Rustenburg in 1876 — twenty-five years before the war, a generation before Johannesburg. Two other notices read the same afternoon sit in the same country: a Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg, born Booyzen , who died at Vaalbank in the district of Lichtenburg in 1920 and whose father is entered as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen ; and an an Anna Johanna Booijzen , born in the district of Cradock about 1823, who died on a farm in the district of Rustenburg in 1891, leaving children called Petrus Jacobus, Magdalena Johanna and Hendrik Stephanus Nicolaas.

charlotta-elizabetha-dormehl.v: Charlotta Elizabeth Roos, geboren Dormehl (1892) · Charlotta Elizabetta Booysen, born Dormehl (1902)
charlotta-elizabetha-dormehl.r: His second wife, married at Zeerust on 14 April 1892 when she was fifty-one and he sixty-three, and her own Death Notice 844 gives the rest: born Graaff-Reinet about October 1841, FARMER'S WIFE, father JACOB DORMEHL and mother UNKNOWN, dead at Driefontein in Groot Marico on 6 February 1902 aged 60 years 4 months, leaving ONE WAGON AND HOUSEHOLD FURNITURE worth £51 8s 0d and a will. THREE HUSBANDS — Jacob van Staden, then Matthys Roos, then Booysen — and SIX CHILDREN, two van Stadens and four Rooses, NOT ONE OF THEM A BOOYSEN. That is why the four children this archive once drew under her are not hers.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: In April 1892 he gives his home as Brakfontein, Rustenburg . He did not leave. The family that this archive spent weeks placing in the north-eastern Cape had a branch sitting on one farm in the Transvaal for at least sixteen years. The 1876 notice → She was a widow, and her name is not what we published This archive has called her Charlotta Elizabetha Dormehl . The register writes Charlotta Elizabeth Roos, geboren Dormehl , condition weduwe , and she signs C. E. Roos geb. Dormehl . Dormehl was her maiden name and Roos was her first husband's. She came to this marriage from Driefontein in Marico with a married name of her own. And he signs with an s The clerk writes him into the register as Booijzen .

ockert-johannes-stephanus-booysen.r: Signed his father’s 1908 death notice as “son of the deceased” — thirty-two years after his father had signed his own father’s at Brakfontein. Second of the seven children on his mother’s 1891 notice, and he carries HER father’s name: Ocken Johannes Oliefier. hits.title: What changed
hits.text: Her father was Jacob Dormehl; her mother is entered UNKNOWN, by a husband of ten years, which makes seven death notices in this archive that fail to name a parent. She had one wagon and her furniture, worth £51 8s 0d, and she left a will. Looking for Ockert's estate and finding his son's Found found Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen died at Klerksdorp on 16 January 1921 and HAS NO ESTATE FILE OF HIS OWN in the indexed Transvaal probate records. Searched under Ockert, Okkert, Ocker and Ocken against Booysen, Booyzen and Booijsen: six hits, every one of them him as somebody else's relative — four duplicate copies of a 1935 Sterfkennis where he is the father, and two of his own father's 1908 notice where he is entered Child.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: There is no b , no r-t-s , and no second syllable that could carry -berts . Oliefier is how a man who writes Booijzen , Stefanes and Brakfontijn spells OLIVIER. And the archive does not have to guess, because her own son wrote her name down again . Seventeen years later, filling in his father's death notice, Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen gave the first wife as "Anna Catharina Johanna Booysen, born Olivier" . The 1908 notice → Three documents, three spellings of one woman: Anna Johanna on her own notice, Anna Catrena on her son's, Anna Catharina Johanna on her husband's. Put together, she is Anna Catharina Johanna Olivier , and every one of them agrees on the surname. Seven children, all of age Question twelve, entire.

hits.text: Not one Booysen among them. Two van Stadens — Jacob Alewyn and Coenrad Sybert . Four Rooses — Gert Johannes , Matthys Johannes , Johannes Sybert , and Anna Francisa , married in community of property to Gert Johannes Laubeschagne. All of age. And after ten years of marriage to Hendrik Stefanus Booysen, no child of his is named , because she was fifty-one when she married him. This archive spent a month drawing his four children under her. Earlier today the 1892 marriage register — her age, her condition — made that impossible. Her own death notice now says the same thing from the other side, in her husband’s handwriting.

diederik-arnoldus-booysen.r: A KARWEIER — a transport rider — of Zwartruggens, and a son of Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen and Elizabeth Johanna Sophia Myburgh. His Sterfkennis 87882 is the first document in this archive printed in Afrikaans rather than Dutch or English, and the first Booysen estate here worth more than £300. He married Elizabeth Anna Bronkhorst, widow Joubert, in community of property; their youngest son carries his grandfather’s name.

anna-catharina-johanna-olivier.v: Anna Johanna Booijzen, gebooren Oliefier (1891) · Anna Catrena (1891) · born Olivier (1908)
anna-catharina-johanna-olivier.r: THE FIRST WIFE OF HENDRIK STEFANUS BOOIJSEN, and for a week this archive had her filed as a stranger. Her own Sterfkennis 6332 gives her parents as OCKEN JOHANNES OLIEFIER and ANNA JOHANNA BOTHA, her age as 67 years 8 months and 1 day, her farm as BRAKFONTEIN — which this archive read as Boekfontein — and her surname as OLIEFIER, which this archive read as Alberts. She was still married when she died: her husband outlived her by seventeen years and remarried at Zeerust eleven months later. Seven children, all of age: Petrus Jacobus, Ocken Johannes, Anna Johanna Maria, Elesabettha Maria Cornelya, Alettha Catrina Johanna, Magdalena Johanna, Hendrick Stefanus Nicolaas. Her father is where OCKERT JOHANNES came into this family — and her 1824 baptism gives his name entire, OCKERT JOHANNES STEPHANUS OLIVIER, which is exactly what her son was called. She married Hendrik Stephanus Booijzen at POTCHEFSTROOM on 3 JULY 1850, entry 206, she 25 and he 23 — the earliest evidence this archive has of this family north of the Vaal, twenty-six years before the 1876 death at Rustenburg and two years before the Sand River Convention.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Not Ocken Johannes , as the 1891 death notice scrawled it. OCKERT JOHANNES STEPHANUS OLIVIER — all three names, exactly as her son carries them. Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen was called after his grandfather, entire. And she had a sister baptised at Cradock eleven months earlier: Aletta Catharina Olivier , 4 October 1823, same parents. Anna Johanna’s own daughter is Aletta Catharina Johanna . The names in this family go back up the female line and this archive could not see it until today. hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Cradock, 4 October 1824 The Cradock doopregister for 1824 — the church her family baptised in, and the district her death notice gives sixty-seven years later. Child Anna Johanna Olivier , born 10 September 1824 Baptised 4 October 1824 , Cradock Father Ockert Johannes Stephanus Olivier Mother Anna Catharina Botha Read her father’s name again. Not Ocken Johannes , as the 1891 death notice scrawled it. OCKERT JOHANNES STEPHANUS OLIVIER — all three names, exactly as her son carries them. Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen was called after his grandfather, entire. And she had a sister baptised at Cradock eleven months earlier: Aletta Catharina Olivier , 4 October 1823, same parents.

anna-maria-van-der-merwe.r: WikiTree makes her a daughter of DAVID SCHALK VAN DER MERWE and ANNA ELIZABETH LOUW—which, if right, is where the forename DAVID SCHALK entered this family: her eldest son carries her father’s names entire.FROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ, and it is checkable against the van der Merwe baptism registers rather than the tree. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — DE VILLIERS HAS HER, AND HE DISAGREES WITH THE TREE. Volume 2 of the Geslacht-register der oude Kaapsche familien, in the van der Merwe genealogy: “(e) 3 WILLEM, gedoopt 30 September 1764, burger te Stellenbosch, gehuwd 7 November 1784 met HESTER MARIA VAN DER MERWE — (f) 1 Johanna Catharina, gedoopt 8 Maart 1787; 2 ANNA MARIA, GEDOOPT 5 OCTOBER 1788, GEHUWD MET PETRUS JACOBUS BOOIJSEN; 3 DAVID SCHALK, GEDOOPT 10 OCTOBER 1790; 4 Hendrina Magdalena, 1792; 5 Hester Maria, 1793; 6 Hendrik Petrus Jacobus, 1796.” SO THE TREE MAKES DAVID SCHALK HER FATHER AND THE BOOK MAKES HIM HER BROTHER, and the two parentages cannot both be right. BUT THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES EITHER READING: on both accounts the name stands one step from her. A BAPTISM DATE AT LAST, AND IT IS FOURTEEN DAYS AFTER HIS — he on 21 September 1788, she on 5 October. His wife, married 1805 at Graaff-Reinet — and DOCUMENTED, which she was not until today. A Dutch Reformed baptism of 4 JANUARY 1807 names her as the mother of DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN, born 12 December 1806, who is FIRST of the eight children on the 1876 Sterfkennis. That resolves a contradiction this archive marked Serious (they were married by 1806, so the 1825 Cape Town marriage record is a different couple) and it rewrites the wall on the ancestor chart, which said only a family tree put her there. WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVED is that she is the mother of the 1812 man in the direct line.

hits.text: One confirmed a guess this archive had already written down; two showed that a researcher had gone out and photographed the wrong building ; and one — the two Gertrudes — turned out not to be an error at all . This archive has also had to correct two mistakes of its own . The documents → The list Person The contradiction Class Reading Anna Maria van der Merwe — whose daughter? The family tree makes her a daughter of DAVID SCHALK VAN DER MERWE and ANNA ELIZABETH LOUW, born 1785. De Villiers's printed Cape genealogy of 1893, volume 2, makes her a daughter of WILLEM VAN DER MERWE and HESTER MARIA VAN DER MERWE, baptised 5 OCTOBER 1788 — fourteen days after the man she married. Both cannot be right.

hits.text: Page 78 then gives her husband as JAN BOOIJSEN, baptised 29 January 1741, and their SEVENTH CHILD as “Petrus Jacobus, gedoopt 21 September 1788, gehuwd met Anna Maria van der Merwe”, whose first child is “David Schalk, gedoopt 4 Januari 1807”. hits.title: Method
hits.text: Seventeen people had a page that said “This person is recorded in the archive’s index but is not yet discussed on any page.” Among them the 1820 Settler , whose name the built site carries 155 times ; John Barry , 158; George Mountjoy , 140; Petrus Jacobus Booysen , 110; Johanna Catharina Mountjoy , 89. What went wrong The gatherer that collects every mention of a person dropped any name that was a strict prefix of a longer person’s name . The rule was written for a good reason — to stop John Barry collecting every mention of John Barry Booyzen — and it was implemented as “delete the shorter man” rather than “let the longer name go first”.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: The women are not. Mountjoy (1838). Barry (1879). Kinnear (1940s). Behind the Barrys, Kolbe — a German tailor's family out of Soho who sailed as 1820 Settlers and named a Karoo farm Wurtemburg . Behind the Kolbes, Downing . That is why David Defranceski's great-grandfather, born on a farm in the Eastern Cape in 1901, was christened George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen . Every one of those forenames is a woman's surname. The women → And it is why the tree folds back on itself: in 1924 George married his own first cousin once removed , so his daughter Catherine descends from one Barry–Kolbe couple twice over. The cousin marriage → Corrections are the most valuable thing anyone can send.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: Resolved RESOLVED. His 1845 death notice (estate 7698) and his gravestone both give 1 December 1844, and neither his notice nor his widow’s 1867 notice lists a Julia. Reject the child, keep the date. The same two documents also drop KEETOR PETER BENJAMIN KOLBE, whom the tree gives a 1840 birth — he is in neither list. → George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen (1901–1947) Death dated 21 February 1947, with burial ten months later on 14 December 1947. Resolved RESOLVED by his death notice: he died 11 December 1947 and was buried on the 14th. “21 February” is the date the notice was signed — in 1948. A transcriber merged the two and lost ten months.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: They are the same woman, and the archive's earlier claim of "two Barry sisters marrying Booysens" is withdrawn . 1947 · George's death notice corrects his own death date Signed by G. Booyzen at Johannesburg on 21 February 1948 under the Administration of Estates Act 1913. Death Notice of George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen , died 11 December 1947 at Forest Hill, Johannesburg. "The day of the decease: On 11th December 1947 " — died at 85 Rheeden St, Forest Hill , Johannesburg. He died on 11 December 1947 — not 21 February 1947. 21 February is the date the notice was signed , and it was signed in 1948 . A transcriber conflated the two and lost ten months.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: There is no photograph of their farm, and this archive does not invent one. This archive was built for David Defranceski , born in Johannesburg, living in Brisbane. It runs backwards from his grandmother Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1929–2013) — who married Nuno Fernando Lerena at St Joseph's, Mayfair, in 1949 — into the north-eastern Cape: to Barkly East and Dordrecht , to Cradock and Graaff-Reinet , and out again to Württemberg , to Soho , and to a County Cork that may or may not be real. It is a public archive with one rule: the living are left out — omitted, not hidden.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: The 1915 death notice shows she is the same woman as Kathleen above. Withdrawn. Read rows five and seven together. Catherina Maria Sophia Barry died on 30 July 1859. Catherine Maria Sophia Barry was born on 4 August 1859 — five days later , and was given the dead child's name. That name then travelled: to Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1891–1946) , and to Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1929–2013) , David Defranceski's grandmother. A four-year-old's death in Burgersdorp is still being commemorated, unknowingly, four generations later.

hits.title: The cousin marriage
hits.text: George was Kathleen's son. Anna was Hendrik's granddaughter. They were first cousins once removed , and their common ancestors are John Augustus Barry I and Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe . What follows from it Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen descends from John Augustus Barry I and Margaretha Kolbe twice — once through her father, once through her mother. This is pedigree collapse : she has fewer distinct ancestors than the arithmetic of generations predicts. Where a person five generations back should have thirty-two separate ancestors, she has thirty — because one couple occupies two of the slots.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: There is no photograph of their farm, and this archive does not invent one. This archive was built for David Defranceski , born in Johannesburg, living in Brisbane. It runs backwards from his grandmother Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1929–2013) — who married Nuno Fernando Lerena at St Joseph's, Mayfair, in 1949 — into the north-eastern Cape: to Barkly East and Dordrecht , to Cradock and Graaff-Reinet , and out again to Württemberg , to Soho , and to a County Cork that may or may not be real. It is a public archive with one rule: the living are left out — omitted, not hidden. And a second rule, which is harder: every claim says how well it is known.

david-schalk-booysen.r: PRISONER OF WAR. A printed transport list in the Pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries THREE CONSECUTIVE BOOYZENS shipped on the CITY OF CAMBRIDGE on 3 JUNE 1901, all entered from PRETORIA: 18463 STEPHANUS FRANCOIS, 28 · 18464 PETRUS JACOBUS, 29 · 18465 DAVID SCHALK, 54. Consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. Age 54 against a birth of 9 June 1848, which would have made him 52 and six days short of 53 when the ship sailed. THE FULLER REGISTER WAS THEN FOUND, and it is better than the De List in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at PRETORIA, riding with the PRETORIA COMMANDO, and TAKEN AT TOLOSBERG ON 25 APRIL 1901. Its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the De List's 28, 29 and 54 did not. If it is him, he was a Transvaal burgher in arms at fifty-two, taken and deported, and he came back — he remarried at Pretoria in November 1905. Fourth on the 1863 list, and THE DIRECT ANCESTOR'S BROTHER — Willem Hermanus is sixth on the same list. For the whole of this project he was a line on that list and nothing else. His wife's 1900 death notice gives him a household: married ELIZABETHA MARGARETHA MARAIS at LADY GREY, the same small Cape church where his brother married Kathleen Barry in 1879; eight children; and by 1900 he was at Pretoria, living in a zinc building in Market Street. He signed her notice there in March 1904 — and on 27 NOVEMBER 1905 he married again at Pretoria, to JOHANNA ELENA STOLS, widow Lowies, of Skinners Court. He was 56, a widower of GOEDE HOOP, PRETORIA, and the register gives his birthplace as CRADOCK. The Remarks column cites his remarriage certificate from the Master, NO. 4795 — which is the number of his first wife’s death notice, so the two documents point at each other and the identification needs no inference. His own death is still not found.
p: A zinc building in Market Street

The 1900 notice calls David Schalk's Stephanus François an unmarried major, which is exactly what this man was. They all belong to one death notice , and it opens a household this archive did not have: the family of David Schalk Booysen , born 9 June 1848 — the brother of the direct ancestor . His parents were JAN LOWIES and ELISABETHA MARIA LUBBE, and he left TWELVE children. THE FILE IS NOW READ. He was a HAWKER, of GOEDEHOOP, PRETORIA — which is the exact address David Schalk Booyzen gave on the marriage register three weeks later, so the two men lived in the same place. Dutch, of the Cradock district, 56 years and 8 months, dead in the LUNATIC ASYLUM at Pretoria on 5 June 1905. Movables but no land, an estate over £100, and a will. hits.text: 7081 is the bride's, and it is CHARLES PETRUS BAREND LOWIES — born in the DISTRICT OF CRADOCK about 1849, dead at PRETORIA on 5 JUNE 1905, parents Jan Lowies and Elisabetha Maria Lubbe, TWELVE children. Read the two men together: David Schalk Booijzen born Cradock 9 June 1848 and widowed at Pretoria in 1900; Charles Petrus Barend Lowies born district Cradock about 1849 and dead at Pretoria in 1905. Two men born a year apart in one Karoo district, both ending in Pretoria — and five months and twenty-two days after the second died, the first married his widow. The Master cleared both estates within four days: 4795 on 4 November, 7081 on the 7th, the wedding on the 27th.

hits.text: 4795 was the groom's and led back to his first wife's death notice. 7081 is the bride's, and it is CHARLES PETRUS BAREND LOWIES — born in the DISTRICT OF CRADOCK about 1849, dead at PRETORIA on 5 JUNE 1905, parents Jan Lowies and Elisabetha Maria Lubbe, TWELVE children. Read the two men together: David Schalk Booijzen born Cradock 9 June 1848 and widowed at Pretoria in 1900; Charles Petrus Barend Lowies born district Cradock about 1849 and dead at Pretoria in 1905. Two men born a year apart in one Karoo district, both ending in Pretoria — and five months and twenty-two days after the second died, the first married his widow.

elizabetha-margaretha-marais.r: His wife, married at Lady Grey near Aliwal North. Daughter of STEPHANUS FRANCOIS MARAIS and ELIZABETHA MARGARETHA MARAIS, born in the district of Cradock about April 1850. She died in a ZINC BUILDING IN MARKET STREET, PRETORIA on 1 June 1900 — four days before Lord Roberts entered the town — and her husband did not file the notice for three years and nine months. Nothing movable left, and a compensation claim filed.
p: A zinc building in Market Street

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: → Stephanus Francois Booyzen (1874–1940) — whose son? This archive placed him as a son of PETRUS JACOBUS BOOYSEN and his second wife JOHANNA MARGARITHA PRETORIUS, on his birth date alone — his own 1940 Sterfkennis names neither parent, because his widow wrote only “oorlede” for both. The 1900 death notice of Elizabetha Margaretha Marais names a STEPHANUS FRANCOIS BOOIJZEN as her son by DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN, an unmarried major at Pretoria in 1904 — and the 1874 man died at East Lynne, Pretoria. Serious 13 September 2026, LATER: his own marriage register adds to the new reading without settling it.

hits.text: Her son is the first David Schalk in this surname. David Schalk Booijsen bapt. 4 Jan 1807 THE FIRST, and the only David Schalk in the whole first volume of the Cape genealogies — the volume that holds every Booijsen de Villiers recorded. David Schalk Booysen b. 9 Jun 1848 The second. Named for his grandfather, four decades on. David Schalk Booijzen the younger c. 1889 The third, youngest on his mother's 1900 notice. David Kolbe Booyzen m. 1921 And it survives beside a second borrowed name: he hyphenated Kolbe onto Booysen and used it as his surname at Port Elizabeth. THE COUNT IS THE ARGUMENT. The three volumes of de Villiers were downloaded as text and the string DAVID SCHALK counted in each.

jan-gerhardus-lodewicus-booysen.r: Seventh on the 1863 list, and carries the name of the man at the top of the line. THIS ARCHIVE HAD HIM DYING IN 1885 AND HAS TAKEN IT BACK: estate TAB MHG O/2899 belongs to his uncle of the same name, born 1818, and the death date was never anything but the estate’s year read backwards onto the wrong man. Nothing is known about what became of him — AND THERE IS NOW ONE PLACE TO LOOK. A JGL BOOYZEN countersigned the money papers of a farm school at KWAGGAFONTEIN, DISTRICT MARICO, through 1898 and into 1899: the subsidy application, the book orders, all four quarterly returns, the writing-off of a £61-6-0 deficit, and a letter arguing that the government had paid £8 too little. The elder man of these initials was thirteen years dead by then. This one would have been forty-two, and Marico adjoins the district his uncle died in. IT IS A CANDIDATE AND NOT AN IDENTIFICATION — the index gives initials, a farm and a post office, and Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus is one of the commonest name-strings in the surname. The file itself would carry a signature.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Since the Transvaal references were first pulled out of NAAIRS, this archive has carried a row saying TAB MHG O/2899 — Jan Gerhardus Lodewikus Booyzen — 1885 , and attached it to the seventh child on the 1863 death notice: Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booysen, born 4 December 1855 . His entry on the people index read "he died in the Transvaal at about thirty." He did not. That sentence had no source except the estate reference itself. The archive read the year off the file number, wrote it into his life as a death date, and then quoted the death date back as if it were evidence.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The dates here make it unmistakable, and this archive keeps the two apart. Five of the eight children of that marriage are named for a parent or a grandparent — the same habit as the Barry names crossing into the Daschners, seen from the other direction and in another family. Johanna Catharina Booysen gets her dates Found found Second on the 1863 death notice and until now nothing but a position in a list. The Dutch Reformed index gives her born 15 May 1844 and baptised at BRAK RIVIER on 4 August 1844 — the farm her father was still on nineteen years later when her mother died there. A small thing, and the kind the register was built to hand over.

gerrit-jacobus-booysen.d: Aug 1951, Middelburg — the day illegible on the stone
gerrit-jacobus-booysen.r: THE STONE IS NOW READ, and it says more than its index line. “IN DANKBARE HULDE AAN ONS GELIEFDE VADER EN OUPA — GERT JACOBUS BOOYZEN — GEB. 19 JAN. 1870 — OORL. 2_ AUG. 1951 — SY GENADE WAS VIR MY GENOEG.” THE BIRTH DAY MATCHES THIS ARCHIVE EXACTLY, and from a source that is not the death notice it came from: 19 January 1870, cut in granite. THE DEATH IS NOW A MONTH instead of a year — AUGUST 1951 — and the day is a 2 followed by a digit this archive cannot read off the photograph, so it is not guessed. VADER EN OUPA: he was a grandfather, which no document here had said. AND THE LAST LINE IS IN THE FIRST PERSON — “His grace was enough for ME” — a widower’s sentence, cut twenty-one years after his wife died. HIS GRAVE IS PHOTOGRAPHED. The eGGSA gravestone library holds “BOOYZEN GERT JACOBUS 1870-1951” in the MIDDELBURG MAIN CEMETERY, Eastern Cape — born 1870 and dead in 1951, which is the year of estate TAB MHG 5155/51, the file this archive has been trying to read on blocked film. He is buried a few stones from his wife. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. The only child entered on his father's 1884 death notice, and born seven years after the first wife died — so a child of the second marriage. He married Isabella Frederika Coetsee at Middelburg on 23 March 1896, and his own son was baptised BOOYZEN, with a z, in 1904.

COETSEE) — GEB. 15 APRIL 1874 — OORL. 31 MAART 1930 — HEMELSE RUS.” HER BIRTH IS NOW A DATE. This archive had “c. May 1874”, worked back from an age; the stone gives 15 APRIL 1874, and an exact date cut on a stone beats a month inferred from an age. THE DEATH MATCHES TO THE DAY — 31 March 1930 — which is a third independent source saying 1930 and not 1943. AND HER GRAVE IS PHOTOGRAPHED: “BOOYZEN ISABELLA FREDERICKA NEE COETSEE 1874-1930”, Middelburg main cemetery, in the eGGSA library. The stone's dates match her own death notice exactly and CONFIRM THE CORRECTION below from a second, independent source — the stone says 1930, not 1943. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. Married Gerrit Jacobus at Middelburg, 23 March 1896. THIS ARCHIVE HAD HER DYING IN 1943 AND HAS TAKEN IT BACK: 1943 is when her husband finally filed, thirteen years after the death. Her notice — KAB 84992, spelled BOOYZEN throughout — names her parents Pieter Coetzee and Isabella Fredrika Coetzee, and three children.

johanna-booyzen.r: NOT THIS FAMILY, and recorded here on purpose. Death notice 6167 — the oldest Booyzen estate paper in the Cape Master's series, and a generation older in form than anything else this archive has read. Widow of Charles du Plessis; one daughter, married to Benjamin Solomon; “no property whatever except a Bond amounting per balance to £15”. Line 3 answers “both dead”. She is here because she was born in 1754 and died in 1843 — the only two dates this archive has for Magdelena Elisabeth de Beer, both off the family tree with no source stated — and because somebody will one day find her and decide she is the same woman. She is not. Her name is not Magdelena, not Elisabeth, and not de Beer.

It belongs on the 1843 Johanna Booyzen notice, against the age given to the day — 89 years, 2 months and 26 days — which is the reading that puts her birth at about 20 March 1754 and is exactly why that notice is dangerous: 1754 and 1843 are the only two dates this archive has for Magdelena Elisabeth de Beer, and they came off a tree with no source. petrus-jacobus-booyzen.r: HIS STONE IS READ AND IT CONFIRMS BOTH DATES EXACTLY: “HIER RUS — MY GELIEFDE SEUN — PIETER J. BOOYZEN — GEB. 29 DES. 1904 — OORL. 7 JUNIE 1937 — NA DIE KRUIS DIE KROON.” Dead at thirty-two. AND ONE WORD OF IT DOES REAL WORK: “MY geliefde seun”, not “ONS”. A stone cut by ONE surviving parent — and his mother Isabella Frederika had been dead seven years when he died, so the parent is his father, GERT JACOBUS, who then lay down beside them both fourteen years later. Three of one household in one cemetery, and the grammar of the inscriptions gives the order they went in. Baptised in the Dutch Reformed register with a Z, son of Gert Jacobus Booyzen and Isabella Frederika Coetzee — the second marriage's line, at Middelburg, spelled Booyzen a year before the Indwe sheet.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The route to their commando and their farm is now mapped and not yet walked. Three Booyzens on a prisoner-of-war transport Found found The family fought. A printed POW transport list in the Pretoria government archives carries three consecutive entries — 18463 Stephanus Francois Booyzen, 28; 18464 Petrus Jacobus Booyzen, 29; 18465 David Schalk Booyzen, 54 — all three shipped on the CITY OF CAMBRIDGE on 3 June 1901, all three from Pretoria. Consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: FamilySearch carries a Dutch Reformed marriage of PETRUS JACOBUS BOOŸZEN and ANNA MARIA VAN DER MERWE dated 9 MARCH 1825, at Cape Town, indexed three separate times. Resolved RESOLVED, 13 September 2026. A Dutch Reformed baptism names DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN, born 12 DECEMBER 1806, as the son of Pieter Jacobus Booijzen and ANNA MARIA VAN DER MERWE — and he is first of the eight on the 1876 Sterfkennis. They were married BY 1806, so the 1805 marriage at Graaff-Reinet stands and the 1825 Cape Town record is a different couple of the same two very common names. It also rewrites the wall on the ancestor chart, which said “only a family tree puts her here”. It no longer does.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: His widow wrote “oorlede” for both parents. Four death notices in this family now ask who the parents were, and four fail. He was a MESSELAAR, a mason, like his half-brother Willem Hermanus at Indwe. The second wife, named — Johanna Margaritha Pretorius Found found The oldest open question in the archive, answered by a christening rather than a death. Every attempt had gone at death notices, which either do not ask for a wife's name or got “oorlede” for an answer.

willem-hermanus-booyzen-of-indwe.v: Booijzen (1907 lidmate register) · William Hermanus (1908 marriage) · William Herman Booyzen (1932)
willem-hermanus-booyzen-of-indwe.d: 29 Jul 1932, Johannesburg Hospital — buried Brixton, grave 6889
willem-hermanus-booyzen-of-indwe.r: AN EIGHTH CHILD, and one this archive did not have. Confirmed at Indwe on 31 May 1907, aged 21, entered “Booijzen”. A MIJNWERKER of DUGMORE MIJN when he married Susanna Adriana Roodt, 16, at Indwe on 21 September 1908 — the only miner in five generations of read occupations, and the answer to the last line of the family testimony. Two children in nine months by two women of the same surname, both entered “onecht”. His mother stood godmother at the first font, which is how this archive knows whose son he is. AND THEN JOHANNESBURG: a WILLIAM HERMAN BOOYZEN, 47, born Cape Province, married, EX MINER UNDERGROUND, of 62 Langford Street, Booysens, died at Johannesburg Hospital on 29 July 1932 of a perforated duodenal ulcer after about one day, and was buried at BRIXTON on 31 July. The occupation, the province, the age within a year and the cemetery all fit; no parents are named, because a civil registration does not ask. And then the grave register closes it: GRAVE 6889 holds “Boysen, William” and, thirty-six years later, SUSANNA ADRIANA BOOYZEN, buried 29 August 1968 — the woman he married at Indwe in 1908. Husband and wife in one grave.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: Grave 6889 closes the second Willem Hermanus Found found The 1932 identification was built on circumstance — ex miner underground, born Cape Province, married, forty-seven, Brixton. The Johannesburg grave register settles it. GRAVE 6889 holds “Boysen, William”, folio 49, and beneath him SUSANNA ADRIANA BOOYZEN, buried 29 AUGUST 1968. Susanna Adriana Roodt is the sixteen-year-old he married at Indwe on 21 September 1908. Husband and wife in one grave, thirty-six years apart. And the clerk spells him BOYSEN — the same spelling an English clerk used for a different man of this family on John Barry's 1915 death notice.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The occupation itself was “told” to the clerk, by a hospital official who wrote the word in brackets. Nobody who knew him was in the room. Grave 6889 — and the identification closes TOWN COUNCIL OF JOHANNESBURG · CONSECUTIVE GRAVE NUMBERS. Grave 6889 : Boysen, William — folio 49; and beneath him Susanna Adriana Booyzen · 29.8.68 . They are in the same grave. Everything above is circumstantial — the occupation, the province, the age, the cemetery. This is not. The Johannesburg grave register puts William Booyzen and Susanna Adriana Booyzen in grave 6889 , thirty-six years apart, and Susanna Adriana Roodt is the woman he married at Indwe on 21 September 1908. Note how the clerk spells him: Boysen .

It now has 26 APRIL 1884 and 23 JANUARY 1952 — the latter matching estate TAB MHG 769/52, a file still unread on a blocked film. “Aan ons vader”: he left children. AND NOW HE HAS A DEATH AND A PLACE. “BOOYZEN JOHN BARRY 1884-1952”, BRENTHURST CEMETERY, BRAKPAN. This archive had him as “c. 1884” with no death at all, and an estate number — TAB MHG 769/52 — on a film that will not open. The stone gives 1884-1952, which matches both the estimate and the estate year, and puts him on the East Rand rather than in Johannesburg. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. Eldest son. Present at his father's death in 1905 and the informant — he signs Booyzen four lines under the clerk's Booysen.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: THE DATA WAS FINE AND THE BUILD THREW IT AWAY. dossiers.py dropped any name that was a strict prefix of a longer person’s name — a rule written to stop “John Barry” swallowing “John Barry Booyzen”, which instead silenced the shorter man entirely. The fix keeps the shorter name and fences it with a negative lookahead, so it matches everywhere except where the longer name begins. 2,428 mentions came back. NOTHING REFUSED THE BUILD WHILE THIS WAS TRUE, so a gate now does: checkregisters.py fails when a person the dossier calls undiscussed is named in the built pages.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: They are not the same word. The clerk, September 1905: Willem Hermanus Boo y sen His son, the same day: J. B. Boo y z en The father is registered under the old spelling. The son signs the new one. Both are on the same page, in September 1905 — three years after the Anglo-Boer War ended. The informant is John Barry Booyzen (b. 1884), the eldest son, then twenty-one, recorded as present at the death . This is as close to a photograph of the surname changing as the archive is ever likely to find. hits.title: Method
hits.text: What went wrong The gatherer that collects every mention of a person dropped any name that was a strict prefix of a longer person’s name . The rule was written for a good reason — to stop John Barry collecting every mention of John Barry Booyzen — and it was implemented as “delete the shorter man” rather than “let the longer name go first”. So the moment anybody added George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom , George Augustus Kolbe stopped existing as far as the build was concerned. Why it is worth a section The data was never wrong. Every record, every document, every citation was intact and on disk the whole time.

david-kolbe-booyzen.r: Carries the Kolbe name three generations after the 1820 Settler — AND HE HYPHENATED IT. The family tree recorded his wife Maria Jacoba Smit, married 1921, under the compound surname KOLBE-BOOYSEN, and this archive filed that as a tree oddity with nothing behind it. The Eastern Province Herald prints it twice. 16 OCTOBER 1944: “SAWTELLE – KOLBY-BOOYSEN. The engagement has been announced between LEVINA (FINNIE), only daughter of Mr and Mrs D. KOLBE-BOOYSEN, of PORT ELIZABETH, to Raymond Patrick, only son of Mrs D. Sawtelle, of Cambridge, England.” 19 APRIL 1945: “KOLBE-BOOYSEN – KRUGER. To be married at St Cuthbert's Church, Bingley Street, Port Elizabeth… Hilda, only daughter of Lieut. and Mrs F. Kruger of Heidelburg, Transvaal, to WILLIAM (S.A.A.F.), son of Mr and Mrs D. KOLBE-BOOYSEN, of Port Elizabeth.” A TOWN AND TWO CHILDREN, from two notices six months apart — and the engagement spells the headline KOLBY and the body KOLBE, four words from each other.

henry-james-booyzen.r: AND NOW THERE IS A REGISTER. The G2G question this archive posted on 13 September was answered within eighteen hours by PIETER VAN ZYL, who put the baptism on the profile: “South Africa, Dutch Reformed Church Registers (Cape Town Archives)”, ark 1:1:6KPT-T3Z4 — HENRY JAMES BOOŸSEN, BORN 12 AUGUST 1887, BAPTISED 27 NOVEMBER 1887, parents WILLEM HERMANUS BOOŸSEN and CATHARINA MARIA SOPHIA BARRY. Verified here against the index directly. The 12 August 1887 has now travelled from a family tree, to a gravestone, to a church register, in that order, which is the wrong way round and is how it usually goes. THE SAME ANSWER ALSO SAYS he was A CARPENTER WHEN HE MARRIED and A RETIRED MINER OF LANGLAAGTE ESTATES when he died, OF PHTHISIS — and this archive has CORONARY PULMONARY SCLEROSIS off the Johannesburg burial register. Phthisis is the Rand miner’s disease and a retired Langlaagte miner dying of it in 1956 is entirely of a piece; but the two causes are not the same word and this archive has read only one of the two documents. REPORTED ON G2G, NOT VERIFIED HERE. AND HIS STONE SETTLES THE BIRTH. WEST PARK, Johannesburg: “HIER RUS — MY DIERBARE EGGENOOT — HENRY JAMES — GEB. 12.8.1887 — OORL. 8.12.1956 — RUS IN VREDE”, over the surname BOOYZEN. The 12 August 1887 this archive carried marked FROM WIKITREE AND NOT FROM A DOCUMENT is now on his own gravestone, and the death matches the burial register to the day. “My dierbare eggenoot” — the stone was raised by his widow, Dorothea Regina. HIS GRAVE IS PHOTOGRAPHED: “BOOYZEN HENRY JAMES 1887-1956”, WEST PARK CEMETERY, Johannesburg — matching the burial register this archive read and the 12 August 1887 birth WikiTree gives. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. A son of Willem Hermanus and Kathleen Barry. WikiTree gives his birth as 12 AUGUST 1887 and his marriage as 17 JUNE 1912 AT ELLIOT, neither of which this archive had—bothFROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ, and the “c. 1887” below is this archive’s own figure, worked back from an age on a burial register. This archive had him as a name on Transvaal estate MHG 10/57 and nothing else — not a birth, not a death. The Johannesburg cemetery register gives all of it: DIED 8 DECEMBER 1956 at the FLORENCE NIGHTINGALE NURSING HOME of CORONARY PULMONARY SCLEROSIS, aged 69, usual residence 3 15TH AVENUE, MAYFAIR — the same suburb where his mother died in 1940 and where his great-niece was married at St Joseph’s in 1949. Buried 12 December in the D.R. section, GRAVE 7110/1, a double plot. In 1912 he married Dorothea Regina Barry, a daughter of his mother's brother Hendrik Nicholaas — the third Barry–Booyzen union in three generations.

richard-peter-booyzen.d: 25 Oct 1918, Turffontein — buried 27 Oct, Brixton, D.R., grave 1119
richard-peter-booyzen.r: TWENTY-FOUR, MARRIED, a SAWYER of 18 Anderson Street, Turffontein — dead of INFLUENZA AND PNEUMONIA after eleven days on 25 October 1918, the centre of Black October, and buried at Brixton on the 27th. Not in this archive before today. Added as a ninth child of Willem Hermanus and Kathleen Barry on three grounds and no document: RICHARD PETER is her own brother's name; a birth about 1894 falls exactly in the gap between her daughter of 1891 and her son of 1901; and his registration gives his birthplace as the CAPE OF GOOD HOPE, which is the migration every one of her children made. A Transvaal death registration names no parents, so this stays INFERRED. And he was NOT A SOLDIER — which kills the best explanation this archive had for his mother's military pension.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: And two infants at Brixton the archive did not have at all. THEN OCTOBER 1918. RICHARD PETER BOOYZEN, twenty-four, buried at Brixton on the 27th — the centre of Black October. This archive has no Richard Peter Booyzen and it should: Richard Peter Barry is Kathleen's own brother, and a boy born about 1894 falls exactly in the gap between her daughter of 1891 and her son of 1901. Added as a ninth child, marked INFERRED, because a burial register names no parents. Two more Booysens went into the same ground within eight weeks and neither can be shown to be kin.

hits.title: What was taken back
hits.text: The FamilySearch collection is titled “Johannesburg Cemetery Records” and the index repeats that label for every register inside it, including those of other municipalities. The collection title is not the place. how A document read wrongly, or a conclusion drawn past what the document says. Where it lives now → 13 Sep 2026 was “Anna J. Mary Booyzen and George Downing Daschner were stillborn or died the same day” now Both lived. She was SIX MONTHS old and he was THREE MONTHS AND FIVE DAYS. The Brixton register keeps Years, Months and Days in three separate columns and FamilySearch's index collapses them into one field, so a child with the Years column blank comes out as “0 days”.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Born Cape Province. Indwe. Married. Since 1908. Forty-seven in July 1932 against twenty-two in September 1908 — which makes him forty-six. One year. Brixton Cemetery, 31 July 1932 , where the burial register gives his birth as 1885 and where this family already buries its Johannesburg dead: Anna J. Mary Booyzen in 1914, John Barry Booyzen in 1916, George Downing Daschner in 1925. And “Sasanna Adriana Booyzen” was buried at Johannesburg in 1968 — his widow, under his name, thirty-six years after him. What does not No parents are named , because a South African civil death registration does not ask for them unless the deceased is under ten.

catharina-maria-sophia-booysen.d: 1946 — West Park, grave 51, beside her husband
catharina-maria-sophia-booysen.r: Baptised at Barkly Oost 24 May 1891, entry 120, named for her mother entire, and fourteen when her father died at Indwe. She married Joseph Heinrich Daschner AT INDWE — the same village — and his 1942 death notice names her “born Booyzen”, with a z, in a Johannesburg typist’s hands. Eleven children, five of them carrying Booyzen and Barry forenames. She died in the Transvaal in 1946 — estate TAB MHG 3734/46, found only when this archive finally searched outside the Cape, and still to be read.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: It does not prove the rebel is Kathleen's brother. It does show that whoever named this child was standing inside the same family this archive is describing. The namesakes → How far the Barry names travel There is no Barry surname left in this family after 1859. There is a great deal of Barry name . The children of Catharina Maria Sophia Booysen — Kathleen Barry's daughter — on her husband's 1942 death notice. Kathleen Barry married a Booyzen in the 1880s, so the surname stops with her. Her daughter married a Daschner, so it is two surnames gone in two generations.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: And a DOUBLE PLOT: Joseph Heinrich Daschner, 58, buried 21 April 1942 in GRAVE 50 of a pair 50/51 he bought himself, with a memorial by L. Canata & Son — and the consecutive grave-number register braces 50 and 51 together, DASCHNER JOSEPH H. and DASCHNER CATHERINE M.S. She is Catharina Maria Sophia Booysen, born 22 April 1891 at Barkly Oost, George's own sister, whose estate MHG 3734/46 is one of the six files in the letter to Pretoria. Four years after he was buried in the first grave she went into the second.

george-downing-daschner.r: THREE MONTHS AND FIVE DAYS old — not “0 days”, which is the index's reading and what this archive printed for an afternoon. The Brixton register keeps Years, Months and Days in three columns. Buried 20 June 1925, D.R. section, grave 4410 — seventeen years before his father went into West Park. A TWELFTH CHILD, and not on the 1942 death notice because he was already dead when it was written. The Johannesburg cemetery index has him buried at Brixton on 20 June 1925, the year he was born. He carries George Downing — the sixth Booyzen or Barry forename to cross into this family, and the one that makes the pattern impossible to read as coincidence. hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: The Barrys stop being a surname in this archive in 1859 and go on being a set of first names for another eighty years. And a sixth, off the 1942 list The Johannesburg cemetery index carries a George Downing Daschner , buried at Brixton on 20 June 1925, the year he was born. He is not on his father's death notice because he was dead seventeen years before it was written — a twelfth child. George Downing is the name of Kathleen Barry's own grandson, born in 1901, and here it is on an infant in another family in the same decade. A second of the name died in 1998.

stephanus-francois-booyzen.r: THE STONE IS NOW READ, and it is the fullest document this archive has for him. SILVERTON, PRETORIA, a double stone under one base reading BOOYZEN: “'n SIMBOOL VAN LIEFDE — AAN MY DIERBARE EGGENOOT EN ONS VADER — STEFANUS FRANCOIS — ✳ 29-9-1874, † 14-5-1940 — Sy plek is leeg, sy stem is stil, ons swyg o'Heer, dit is Gods wil. Ges. 75:1”. HIS BIRTH IS NOW EXACT: 29 SEPTEMBER 1874, where this archive had only “c. October 1874”. And a pillar between the two halves lists TWELVE CHILDREN by their household names — OUBOET · OUSIE · BESSIE · BETIE · HENNA · EVERT · ✝BABA · FANIE · WILLIE · PIETIE · JOHAN · HENNIE — one of them marked dead with a cross. This archive had almost none of them. They are nicknames, not names on a register, and nothing is claimed from them beyond the count. HIS GRAVE IS FOUND AND PHOTOGRAPHED: “BOOYZEN STEFANUS FRANCOIS 1874-1940”, SILVERTON MAIN CEMETERY, PRETORIA — a joint stone with his wife, “BOOYZEN BEATRIX MAGDALENA CATHARINA NEE BOSHOFF 1889-1977”. Both dates match this archive exactly, and hers is the first death year it has had for her. He died at East Lynne, Pretoria, and lies at Silverton. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. PRISONER OF WAR. A printed transport list in the Pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries THREE CONSECUTIVE BOOYZENS shipped on the CITY OF CAMBRIDGE on 3 JUNE 1901, all entered from PRETORIA: 18463 STEPHANUS FRANCOIS, 28 · 18464 PETRUS JACOBUS, 29 · 18465 DAVID SCHALK, 54. Consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. Age 28 against this archive's c. October 1874, which would have made him 26. THE FULLER REGISTER WAS THEN FOUND, and it is better than the De List in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at PRETORIA, riding with the PRETORIA COMMANDO, and TAKEN AT TOLOSBERG ON 25 APRIL 1901. Its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the De List's 28, 29 and 54 did not. AND THEN THE PRISONER NUMBER LED SOMEWHERE ELSE ENTIRELY. The medal-roll database at angloboerwar.com holds an entry for a STEPHANUS FRANCOIS BOOYSEN, BURGER, whose PoW number is 18463 — the same number as the register — and it says he was a ZARP, one of the ZAR's police, based at PRETORIA. Quoting a City Coins auction catalogue of November 2020 that described his ABO medal and the papers with it: in action at TALANA, MODDER SPRUIT, COLENSO, PLATRAND (WAGON HILL) where he was WOUNDED IN THE RIGHT LEG ABOVE THE KNEE, SPION KOP and DALMANUTHA — the ZARPs' famous last stand. His applications were completed by his commanding officer, COMMANDANT J. P. DE LA C. SCHROEDER. He was one of FORTY-TWO Boers taken at Tolosberg in the Waterval Valley on 25 April 1901, with two guns and much stock, and was sent to INDIA. This archive has NOT seen the medal or the application; it is strong secondary evidence tied to the register by the number and not by the name. WHAT IT DOES TO THE DISPUTE: he is numbered 18463 and David Schalk Booysen is 18465, two apart on the same transport on the same day, and this man died at EAST LYNNE, PRETORIA, which is the district all three were taken in. That is a FOURTH point favouring David Schalk as his father, and the first that does not depend on a forename. It is still not a document naming a parent. PARENTAGE DISPUTED — see below. A son of the second marriage, and a MESSELAAR — a mason, like his half-brother Willem Hermanus at Indwe. david-schalk-booyzen-of-1940.r: AND THE ESTATE INDEX AGREES WITH THE STONE, which is what moves him from inferred to documented: “MHG 7653/66 — BOOYZEN, DAVID SCHALK, 1966”. The stone gives an initial and a year; the estate index gives the name in full and the same year. Two collections that do not speak to each other, found an hour apart. OUBOET ON THE SILVERTON PILLAR, and now a grave: “BOOYZEN DAVID S. 1907–1966 & RACHEL M. 1909–1973”, Zandfontein cemetery, Pretoria. The initial, the forename, the town and a birth two years after his parents’ 1905 marriage all agree, and he is the only David S. Booyzen in the Gauteng collection. IT IS A MATCH ON A NAME AND A DATE, NOT A DOCUMENT, and it is marked inferred for that reason. FROM THE INDEX; no image read. Eldest named on his father's 1940 estate — and a name that matters. If Stephanus Francois is DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN's son, as the 1900 death notice suggests, then this boy is called after his grandfather outright. Under the reading this archive published instead, he is called after a great-uncle. It is a point in the argument and not a proof.

hits.text: EVERT Ewert Philippus Booyzen The same name, spelt as the family said it ✝ BABA Nobody A TWELFTH CHILD. Cut with a birth star and a cross and no name at all — baba is simply baby . Not on the 1940 estate because the child was already dead when it was written. FANIE Stephanus Francois Booyzen the younger Fanie ← Stefanus. Standard, and unambiguous. That is what makes the twelfth real.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Not on the 1940 estate because the child was already dead when it was written. FANIE Stephanus Francois Booyzen the younger Fanie ← Stefanus. Standard, and unambiguous. WILLIE Willem Hendrik Booyzen Willie ← Willem PIETIE Petrus Jacobus Booyzen Pietie ← Petrus JOHAN Johan Abraham Frederik Booyzen The same name HENNIE Hendrik Rudolph Philippus Booyzen Hennie ← Hendrik Eleven names on the estate, twelve on the stone, and every one of the eleven is claimed exactly once. That is what makes the twelfth real. Nine of the matches are ordinary Afrikaans diminutives; two — ouboet and ousie — are not names but places in the family, and they fall to the two children the diminutives leave over.

baba-booyzen.r: A TWELFTH CHILD, AND THE ONLY WORD CUT FOR HER OR HIM IS “BABA”. The centre pillar of the Silverton stone lists twelve children by their household names; the 1940 estate lists eleven by their registered ones; and when the two are set side by side EVERY ONE OF THE ELEVEN IS CLAIMED EXACTLY ONCE, leaving “✝ BABA” — a birth star, a cross, and no name — with nothing to match. Not on the estate because the child was already dead when it was written. NO DATE, NO SEX, NO NAME, NO ORDER beyond the stone's own. This archive has met the shape before: Joseph Heinrich Daschner's 1942 notice named eleven children and the Brixton register produced a twelfth. A death notice lists the living; a gravestone, cut by the family, lists the children.

No birth date, no sex, no order of birth beyond the stone's own order, and no name — the child is entered here as Baba Booyzen because that is the only word cut for it. The matches above are readings of nicknames, not documents, and the household page marks every one of them as inferred rather than stated. hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: If he is David Schalk Booijzen’s son, that boy is called after his grandfather outright; under the reading this archive published, he is called after a great-uncle. Two of the eleven — Ewert Philippus and Susanna Fredrika Aletta — are called straight after his WIFE’S parents, Evert Philip Boshoff and Susanna Frederika Aletta Meyer, which shows this couple did name children after grandparents. The naming argues for the new reading: her father was STEPHANUS FRANCOIS MARAIS, which is exactly where the forename would come from, and there is no Stephanus Francois anywhere in the Pretorius side.

hits.text: OUSIE Susanna Fredrika Aletta Booyzen Not a name either: ousie , eldest sister. Matched by position — and she is the only daughter left over once the other three are matched by name. BESSIE Elizabeth Magrieta Booyzen Bessie ← Elizabeth BETIE Beatrix Magdalena Catharina Booyzen Betie ← Beatrix — her mother's name entire HENNA Johanna Catharina Booyzen Henna ← Johanna. The weakest of the nine: Henna can also stand for Hendrina, and there is no Hendrina on the estate. EVERT Ewert Philippus Booyzen The same name, spelt as the family said it ✝ BABA Nobody A TWELFTH CHILD. Cut with a birth star and a cross and no name at all — baba is simply baby . Not on the 1940 estate because the child was already dead when it was written.

james-montjoy.r: Saddler. Owned a house and erf at Cradock worth £90. His 1840 death notice gives his parents as NOT KNOWN — the oldest document here, and the top of this line. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — A MAN WHO SLEPT IN HIS HOUSE SAYS WHERE HE CAME FROM. John Montgomery, founder of Burgersdorp, in The Friend of the Free State of 25 November 1869, recalling his arrival at Cradock in January 1822 when the place held about six people: “Messrs. SOLOMON and S.M. DE BEER, the Rev. Mr. EVANS, Mr. P. GIE, JAMES MOUNTJOY (A SADDLER, WHO WAS DISCHARGED FROM THE 21ST LIGHT DRAGOONS), the two Messrs. ZIERVOGEL, Mr. HEILBERG, Fieldcornet B.J. VORSTER, and Gert VAN DEVENTER. After some trouble I obtained lodgings for the night from Mr. MOUNTJOY.” THERE IS NO ROOM IN A VILLAGE OF SIX FOR TWO SADDLERS OF ONE NAME. The 21st Light Dragoons were the cavalry of the Cape garrison from the 1806 expedition until the end of that decade, so HE ARRIVED IN UNIFORM — which is exactly why no Cape document can say where he was from, and why the marriage register of 1817 rules a line through the column and leaves it empty. He was not a passenger on anything. THE RECORD THAT ANSWERS IT IS WO 97 AT KEW, the Chelsea discharge papers, arranged by regiment before 1855, which give a soldier's PARISH AND COUNTY OF BIRTH, his age at enlistment and his trade. 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 — HIS DISCHARGE NOW HAS A DEADLINE, AND IT CAME FROM THE LONDON PAPERS. The 21st Light Dragoons were relieved at York in MAY 1806 and sailed from Portsmouth for the Cape; part of them went on to SOUTH AMERICA in 1806 and came back to the Cape in 1807; Parliament complained in MARCH 1809 that they had been sent “WHERE THEY COULD HAVE NOTHING TO DO”; a large reinforcement followed in OCTOBER 1810; SIR JOHN CRADOCK reviewed them and pronounced them “IN THE HIGHEST STATE OF DISCIPLINE”; a DRAFT OF 140 MEN embarked for the Cape in OCTOBER 1813; and then, in a letter from the Cape dated 1 AND 10 SEPTEMBER 1817 and printed in five London papers that November, “THE 21ST LIGHT DRAGOONS HAVE EMBARKED FOR INDIA”. HE MARRIED AT GRAAFF-REINET ON 9 MARCH 1817. HIS REGIMENT SAILED FOR INDIA SIX MONTHS LATER. A man who married in March 1817 and was keeping a house and a saddler's trade at Cradock by January 1822 was discharged at the Cape BEFORE SEPTEMBER 1817, and what he was choosing between was a wife at Graaff-Reinet and a transport to Madras. THE TOWN HE SETTLED IN IS NAMED AFTER THE GOVERNOR WHO REVIEWED HIS REGIMENT.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: Both of them lie under a cut-stone monument at Burgersdorp — names, London birthplaces, farm and dates carved into it — about forty miles from where that notice was written. The family forgot them inside seventy years, with the headstone still standing. And it had happened before, on the other side of the house. In 1840 a relative of James Montjoy filled in the same printed form at the same box. He knew the dead man's trade, his house, what it was worth, the village he died in and the name of his wife's first husband. Where it asked for the parents, he wrote: "Names of the Parents of the Deceased. Not Known ." — and for birth-place, only "Europe" . James Montjoy had died thirteen years earlier .

hits.title: Errands
hits.text: John Montgomery, who lodged in his house at Cradock in January 1822, describes JAMES MOUNTJOY as “a saddler, WHO WAS DISCHARGED FROM THE 21ST LIGHT DRAGOONS”. James Montjoy's own death notice answers the question “names of the parents of the deceased” with NOT KNOWN, and his 1817 marriage register rules a line through the column that should say where he came from. Nobody at the Cape knew, because he did not arrive as a settler — he arrived in uniform. The army knew.

anna-catharina-sleer.r: Lived to ninety-eight. Married James Montjoy 9 Mar 1817 at Graaff-Reinet, having first been the widow of a Pietersen. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — SHE HAS PARENTS, A BAPTISM AND THREE SIBLINGS. De Villiers's volume 3, entry 876: “WILLEM SLIER, VAN HAMBURG, gehuwd 19 November 1780 met ANNA CATHARINA FORTMAN — (b) 1 ANNA CATHARINA, GEDOOPT 14 OCTOBER 1787, GEHUWD MET HERMANUS PIETERSE; 2 Wilhelmina Christina, gedoopt 27 December 1789, gehuwd 5 Januari 1811 met Jan Abraham van Wijk, van Amsterdam; 3 Geertruida Johanna, gedoopt 2 Juli 1791; 4 Wilhelmus Josephus, gedoopt 5 Maart 1797.” AND THE FIVE SPELLINGS STOP BEING A MYSTERY: a Hamburg name — Schlier, Schleer — written down by Cape clerks who had never seen it. She married Hermanus Pietersen on 5 APRIL 1807 at nineteen, was a widow by March 1817, a widow again by September 1827, and lived until 1885. FIFTY-EIGHT YEARS A WIDOW.

willem-slier.r: HER FATHER, AND HALF OF A NAME THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN TRACKING FOR WEEKS. Of Hamburg; married ANNA CATHARINA FORTMAN on 19 NOVEMBER 1780 at the Cape; four children baptised between 1787 and 1797. His grandson, baptised in 1809, is WILLEM Hermanus Pietersen — Willem for this man and Hermanus for the boy's own father — and that is the whole derivation of a name two Booyzens in the direct line would later carry. HALF OF IT IS GERMAN AND NONE OF IT IS BOOYZEN BLOOD.

hermanus-pietersen.r: ANNA CATHARINA SLIER'S FIRST HUSBAND, AND UNTIL TODAY THIS ARCHIVE HAD HIM AND HIS SON AS ONE MAN. De Villiers, volume 3: “HERMANUS PIETERSEN, NAMEN VAN OUDERS ONBEKEND, gehuwd 5 APRIL 1807 met ANNA CATHARINA SLIER — (b) 1 Willem Hermanus, gedoopt 12 Maart 1809; 2 Johan Christiaan, gedoopt 28 April 1810.” The entry here used to read “Willem Hermanus Pieterzen, her first husband”, built from two documents that spell him differently — the 1817 marriage register's HARMANUS PIETERZE and the 1840 death notice's WILLIAM PIETERSEN — and two spellings looked like one long name. THEY ARE A FATHER AND A SON. His own parents were unknown to the book, as James Montjoy's would be to the clerk ten years later: TWO MEN IN ONE WOMAN'S LIFE AND NEITHER OF THEM HAD A RECORDED FATHER.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: That was wrong, and it was corrected on 15 September 2026. Corrected from the printed genealogy De Villiers gives “Hermanus Pietersen, namen van ouders onbekend, gehuwd 5 April 1807 met Anna Catharina Slier” and their sons as Willem Hermanus (1809) and Johan Christiaan (1810) . The husband is Hermanus ; the 1851 godfather is his son , which this page already said in the line above without following it. The 1840 notice is the odd one out.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: A third indexing, under the spelling Montyoy , did. Graaff-Reinet marriage register, folios 60–61. "Den 9 Maart 1817 getrouwd" — married on 9 March 1817. The entry, with a pencil cross beside it: "James Montjoy — Met · Anna Catharina Slier, weduwe van Harmanus Pieterze[n]" What it does not say, and that is the point This archive went to this register expecting an origin . Cape marriage entries of this date routinely record where a party came from, and this very page does it repeatedly — three couples in the right-hand column are entered "beide van Uitenhage" . Against James Montjoy's name there is a long ruled dash and nothing else .

hits.title: The Name
hits.text: Five spellings of one woman are a fact about handwriting. Two spellings of one surname are supposed to be a fact about history. The difference is that somebody in this family cared about the second one. And the same page gives the other half of the pattern. Her son was baptised Willem Hermanus Pietersen in 1809; the 1851 Graaff-Reinet register writes the surname Pieterzen , twice, in the hand that wrote Booyzen three lines above. The Pietersens changed nothing either. What the name means A patronymic Booysen is Dutch and means "son of Booy" . Booy is itself a short form of Boudewijn — the Dutch form of Baldwin , from Germanic bald ("bold") and win ("friend").

willem-hermanus-pietersen.r: THE SON, not the husband — and the man the name in this family actually comes from. Baptised 12 March 1809, the elder of Anna Catharina Slier's two Pietersen boys, and so HALF-BROTHER to the Montjoy children. He stood godfather at the 1851 Graaff-Reinet font, where his surname is written PIETERZEN twice in the same hand that wrote BOOYZEN three lines above — the entry that taught this archive that a z is Dutch orthography and not intent. HIS NAME IS HIS TWO GRANDFATHERS AND HIS FATHER: WILLEM for Willem Slier of Hamburg, HERMANUS for Hermanus Pietersen.

hits.text: What has changed is that the one false positive has been opened and turns out to be his mother-in-law. So the van Niekerks are now documented. hits.title: The documents
hits.text: So the van Niekerks are now documented. Maria Sophia van Niekerk , who married Hercules Johannes Mountjoy at Dordrecht on 8 October 1888, was a daughter of Jan Dirk Abram Frans van Niekerk and Carolina Deybella Margrietta Alletta Botha , who was herself born in the district of Cradock and whose parents were Philip Rudolph Botha and a mother of the same long name. Her ten brothers and sisters were Carolina Deybella Margrietta Alletta, Cornelius, Maria Francina Cecilia (widow of Gert Olivier), Jan Dirk Abram Frans, Hercules Johannes , Christiaan Jacobus, Cornelia Elizabeth Gertruida (married James Ross), Benjamin Jacobus, Pieter Jacobus and Philip Rudolph.

hits.text: William Herman Daschner , who was a name on his father's 1942 notice and nothing else, is MHG 2703/63 in the estate index and “DASCHNER Willie 1915–1963” on a West Park stone. The index gives the registered name and the year; the stone gives the household name and the same year. Fritz Johannes Mountjoy , baptised at Barkly East in 1894, lies in Barkly East main cemetery, 1893–1973. Neither was found by looking for him. Both fell out of sweeping a surname. A method note, because it cost an hour. NAAIRS treats two keywords as OR unless the operator between them is sent explicitly. BARRY with BURGERSDORP returned 6,245 documents — more than BARRY alone — and looked for a moment like a rich seam.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: She died at Wodehouse on 25 October 1897, aged fourteen months. On 8 November 1901 they had another daughter and gave her the whole name again; she married Hendrik Stefanus Palm, and a granddaughter born in 1920 carries it still. Replacement naming is well attested in these congregations and is exactly how a records-matcher invents one person out of two. The dates here make it unmistakable, and this archive keeps the two apart.

john-barry.r: One profile holding two men — and on 14 September 2026 they came apart. THE YORKSHIRE MAN IS NOW A LIFE: born at WHITBY in 1796; resident at BILSDALE MIDCABLE when he took a licence on 2 October 1838 to marry MARGARET JACKSON of Beadlam at Helmsley; and in the 1851 census a SHIP OWNER at SHIP YARDS, RUSWARP, WHITBY, aged 55, married, head of his household — the ONLY John Barry of that age in the whole Yorkshire census. John Barry deaths are then registered in the WHITBY district in 1858 and in 1860. He outlived the Cape man, who died at de Bruins Poort in 1853, by at least five years. THEY ARE TWO MEN. What this archive still does not have is the Cape one: no birth, no arrival, no burial. And a caution worth keeping — a Whitby SHIP OWNER is exactly the kind of man whose son could be born AT SEA, which is what John Augustus Barry's death notice says of 1819. That coincidence is not evidence, and the censuses say it is not the same man.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: THE DATA WAS FINE AND THE BUILD THREW IT AWAY. dossiers.py dropped any name that was a strict prefix of a longer person’s name — a rule written to stop “John Barry” swallowing “John Barry Booyzen”, which instead silenced the shorter man entirely. The fix keeps the shorter name and fences it with a negative lookahead, so it matches everywhere except where the longer name begins. 2,428 mentions came back.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: Either the death date was derived from this very record by someone reading it as an end rather than a beginning, or the 1825 marriage is a different couple entirely — Cape Town is six hundred miles from Graaff-Reinet, and both names are common. The archive is not going to guess which. → John Barry (1796–1853) Buried at St Hilda's, Bilsdale, Yorkshire on 3 January 1853 — and dies at de Bruins Poort, Eastern Cape, on 8 January 1853, five days later. Fatal Two men merged. A Yorkshire farmer of Bilsdale (christened 1796, at Holly Bower in the 1841 and 1851 censuses, buried at St Hilda's) has been welded to a John Barry who died in the Cape. Separate them.

hits.title: The cousin marriage
hits.text: The Schoemans sit alongside the Barrys in the same way. P. Schoeman witnessed the 1879 Booysen–Barry marriage ; Anna Johanna Maria Schoemann married Hendrik Nicholaas Barry in 1877; and the 1901 Pretorius–Barry wedding was held at the home of D. Schoeman . Why that matters → The names give it away Anna's mother was christened Margarietha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Barry — the same four names, in the same order, as her own grandmother Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe . And Anna herself was "named after Anna Johanna Maria Schoemann" , her father's mother, a fact the tree records explicitly rather than leaving to be inferred.

richard-pieter-kolbe-barry.r: AND THE NAME IS IN A GOVERNMENT FILE, TWICE OVER, IN ONE LINE. SAB, VWR volume 2, reference B645/8/38, 1937: “AANSOEK DEUR PLAASEIENAAR BARKLY-OOS. RPK BARRY. BYWONER RPK BARRY (SEUN).” An application by a farm owner at Barkly East — R.P.K. BARRY — and the bywoner on the place is R.P.K. BARRY, HIS SON. TWO MEN OF THESE INITIALS AT BARKLY EAST IN 1937, one holding the land and one working it as a tenant, and the state file is between them. This archive cannot say which of the two is the man born in 1899 and does not guess. A BYWONER is not a labourer and not an owner; it is the word South Africa used in the 1930s for a white tenant farming another man's ground, and VWR is the Department of Social Welfare. THE FILE HAS NOT BEEN READ. CARRIES BOTH NAMES AT ONCE — Richard Pieter, for the Barry of Manorowen, and Kolbe, for the 1820 Settler family his great-grandmother married out of. johanna-catharina-mountjoy-of-indwe.r: She joined the Dutch Reformed congregation at Indwe on 23 JULY 1907, arriving FROM BARKLY OOST — six weeks after Willem Hermanus Booijzen was confirmed in the same church — and the register’s last column records her dead there in June 1911. A Mountjoy and a Booyzen in one small colliery congregation, twenty-two years after the two families stood at the same font at Barkly Oost. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND THERE IS NOW A CANDIDATE BIRTH DATE, NOT ENTERED. The baptism transcriptions indexed by gendatabase.com hold a JOHANNA CATHARINA MOUNTJOY BORN 28 JANUARY 1860, one of four Mountjoy children baptised between 1858 and 1864. She would be FIFTY-ONE in June 1911. IT IS NOT BEING TAKEN: this family already contains a Johanna Catharina Mountjoy born 1819, so the name repeats within it, and WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT IS THE CONGREGATION THE 1860 BAPTISM WAS REGISTERED IN — which is the field that site charges for. If it is Barkly East or its district, the two women are almost certainly one.

A Johanna Catharina Mountjoy born 28 January 1860 would be fifty-one in June 1911. It is a candidate and it is not being entered.

william-henry-keys.r: Married JOHANNA CATHARINA MOUNTJOY, baptised at Burgersdorp on 29 February 1860 — a daughter of George Mountjoy and Maria Sophia Botha, which this archive had been asking about and can now answer. Eight children baptised across Dordrecht, Barkly East and Barkly West between 1878 and 1898: Robert Byron, William Henry, JAMES JONATHAN, George, Lancelott Byron, Cecil Frederik, Rachel Anna Maria and HERKLAAS EDWARD JOHANNES. The Mountjoy forenames crossing into a third surname, exactly as the Barry names crossed into the Daschners — and BYRON twice, which appears nowhere else in this archive.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The baptism registers name eight, and the places track the family across the border — Graaff-Reinet 1858, Burgersdorp 1860, Smithfield in the Orange Free State 1862 and 1864. One of the eight answers an open question: JOHANNA CATHARINA MOUNTJOY, baptised at Burgersdorp on 29 FEBRUARY 1860, a leap day, is the woman who married William Henry Keys and put Mountjoy forenames into a third surname. A Petronella Christina Aletta baptised at Swellendam in 1871 carries both parents' names and is NOT adopted: Swellendam is six hundred miles west of anywhere else this family stood.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Swellendam is six hundred miles west and this archive does not accept that one; the parents’ names match and the geography does not. And the Keys question is answered. This site has carried a William Henry Keys who married a Johanna Catharina Mountjoy and baptised children at Dordrecht, Burgersdorp and Barkly East between 1878 and 1898 — among them James Jonathan Keys and Herklaas Edward Johannes Keys , Mountjoy forenames crossing into a third surname. It has been asking which Johanna Catharina Mountjoy. This one.
